entries.email_summary: Strive posts $509M GAAP Q3 profit on BTC gains, but dilution continues as Fidelity's stake shrinks to 8.1% and B.Riley trims price target.
entries.bottom_line: Q3 results show real execution on the Bitcoin-yield story (18.5% QTD, 63.2% YTD, 43,124 BTC) and a large GAAP profit, but share count growth, a cut price target, and an agent exiting the ATM program underscore ongoing dilution and valuation caution. Net effect on thesis is roughly neutral this week.
source_conflicts: BTC holdings cited as 43,124 in Strive's official Q3 press release/8-K, while several trackers (DefiLlama, mNAV.com) round to 43,000 BTC as of early November.

updates.headline: Strive posts $509M GAAP Q3 profit on BTC gains
updates.what_happened: Strive's Q3 2026 earnings release reported GAAP net income of $509 million and diluted EPS of $5.24, driven by $533.7 million in unrealized bitcoin gains, versus revenue of only $2.70 million. The company disclosed BTC Yield of 18.5% for the quarter and 63.2% year-to-date, having acquired 8,136 BTC in Q3 and a further 15,124 BTC from Oct 1-30, bringing total holdings to 43,124 BTC, alongside $490.4 million cash and a completed $609 million net SATS preferred raise on October 20.
updates.thesis_fit: Strong BTC yield and a large unrealized-gain-driven profit support the Bitcoin-per-share growth story central to the treasury thesis, though revenue remains negligible versus the core operating business.

updates.headline: Fidelity's passive stake in ASST falls to 8.1%
updates.what_happened: A Schedule 13G/A (Amendment No. 2) filed by FMR LLC and Abigail Johnson showed their jointly reported stake falling to 8.1% (9,514,519 shares) as of October 30, 2026, down from 13.8% (9,887,332 shares) reported as of June 30, 2026. The percentage decline stems mainly from a near-doubling of shares outstanding (implied ~117.5 million from ~71.6 million) rather than large share sales by Fidelity.
updates.thesis_fit: The sharp percentage drop in a major passive holder's stake, driven by rapid share-count growth from ATM issuance, is a concrete marker of the dilution risk central to the thesis.

updates.headline: Benchmark Company to exit ASST's ATM sales agreements
updates.what_happened: Two 424B3 filings disclosed that The Benchmark Company, LLC will exit as a sales agent from both Strive's up to $2.55 billion Class A common stock ATM program and its up to $2.6 billion SATA preferred ATM program, effective November 16, 2026, with the other existing agents remaining in place.
updates.thesis_fit: A single agent exiting a multi-bank ATM syndicate is a routine administrative change and does not by itself alter financing capacity or dilution terms.

updates.headline: B.Riley cuts ASST price target to $27 from $33
updates.what_happened: B.Riley lowered its price target on Strive to $27 from $33 while maintaining a Buy rating, citing a lower Bitcoin price assumption and a larger preferred equity stack; the firm raised its 2026 BTC holdings estimate to ~47,000 and its preferred-stack projection to $2.4 billion, while cutting its EV/mNAV multiple to 1.6x from 1.7x.
updates.thesis_fit: A price-target cut tied explicitly to a growing preferred stack reinforces the risk that rising senior claims could dilute the common equity's Bitcoin-per-share upside.

entries.email_summary: No material new filings in the last 3 days; secondary sources estimate another ~$86M SATA raise funding ~1,000 more BTC, unconfirmed by 8-K.
entries.bottom_line: No new primary-source disclosures emerged in the last three days beyond the already-reported 26,355 BTC purchase and TD Cowen upgrade. Secondary trackers estimate Strive raised roughly $86M via SATA sales from Sept 21-23, which if confirmed would extend the accumulation pace but has not yet been disclosed in an 8-K.
source_conflicts: Estimated SATA capital raise of ~$85.88M (Sept 21-23) and implied ~1,002 BTC purchase are based on third-party BitcoinTreasuries.net modeling, not yet confirmed by a Strive 8-K filing.

updates.headline: Trackers estimate ~$86M SATA raise, no 8-K yet
updates.what_happened: Secondary crypto-news outlets citing BitcoinTreasuries.net estimated that Strive raised roughly $85.88 million through SATA preferred stock sales over three trading sessions from September 21-23, 2026, which could fund purchase of approximately 1,002 more bitcoin. As of these reports, Strive's last confirmed SEC filing still showed 26,355 BTC as of September 18, with no new 8-K disclosing an updated bitcoin count.
updates.thesis_fit: Continued reliance on the SATA ATM to fund accumulation supports the Bitcoin-per-share growth story, but the figure is an unconfirmed third-party estimate pending the company's next official balance-sheet update.

entries.email_summary: TD Cowen hikes ASST price target to $44 on faster BTC accumulation; no new dilution or governance red flags this window.
entries.bottom_line: The only new development this window is a sell-side price target increase reinforcing the accumulation-driven bull case already priced into recent 8-Ks; no new financing, dilution, or governance issues emerged beyond items already reported.
source_conflicts: Intraday ASST price quotes on 2026-09-22 varied slightly across sources ($29.68 on Robinhood vs. $29.97 on Investing.com vs. $29.66 on Yahoo real-time), likely reflecting different snapshot times rather than a data conflict.

mNAV figures (1.25x basic / 1.68x diluted per bitcointreasuries.net) are dated Sep 14, 2026 and predate the latest 1,355 BTC purchase and subsequent share price rally, so current mNAV is likely different and should be treated as stale.

updates.headline: TD Cowen raises ASST price target to $44 from $32
updates.what_happened: TD Cowen analysts Lance Vitanza and Jonnathan Navarrete lifted their price target on ASST, citing bitcoin accumulation that has outpaced their model and stronger growth in bitcoin held per fully diluted share. The firm now projects Strive will end 2026 with 32,105 BTC (up from a prior 27,156 estimate) and raised its full-year BTC Yield forecast from 54.1% to 70.1%.
updates.thesis_fit: A raised sell-side target grounded in accelerating BTC-per-share growth supports the thesis that Strive can build a durable, market-trusted Bitcoin-per-share story.

updates.headline: Strive CEO discusses bitcoin outlook on Bloomberg Crypto
updates.what_happened: Strive Chairman/CEO Matt Cole appeared on Bloomberg Crypto to discuss the broader digital-asset market, which had reclaimed roughly $3 trillion in value amid a bitcoin rally, alongside growing use of leveraged perpetual futures by traders. The segment was general market commentary rather than a company-specific disclosure.
updates.thesis_fit: Routine media commentary from management with no new treasury, financing, or governance information; does not change the thesis.

entries.email_summary: Strive bought another 1,355 BTC ($107.7M) to reach 26,355 BTC, funded partly by newly-active warrant exercises alongside SATA preferred sales.
entries.bottom_line: Strive continued its weekly accumulation cadence, adding 1,355 BTC and diversifying financing with $21.2M of warrant-exercise proceeds alongside SATA preferred sales, which modestly eases reliance on dilutive preferred issuance. Continued share-count growth and an elevated market premium to Bitcoin NAV keep dilution and valuation-support risk as the key swing factors for the thesis.

snapshot.holdings: 26,355 BTC as of September 18, 2026 (up from 25,000 BTC reported the prior week)

source_conflicts: mNAV/premium figures vary by source and date: mnav.com cites 1.67x (as of ~21,356 BTC, three weeks old), an M1 summary cites 1.69x, and Yahoo Finance references a '90% NAV premium' tied to the 25,000 BTC disclosure — no single up-to-date mNAV figure could be confirmed for the 26,355 BTC holding as of Sept 18-21.

updates.headline: Strive buys 1,355 BTC for $107.7M, holdings hit 26,355
updates.what_happened: Strive disclosed via 8-K that it purchased 1,355 bitcoin between September 14 and September 18, 2026 at an average price of about $79,475 per coin, inclusive of fees, taking total holdings to 26,355 BTC. Class A common shares outstanding rose by 2,073,760 to 87,804,613 and cash grew to $229.6 million, a $25.4 million increase from September 11, while SATA preferred shares outstanding rose by 786,194 to 11,184,160.
updates.thesis_fit: Continues the core Bitcoin-accumulation narrative that underpins the treasury-wrapper thesis, but the accompanying rise in Class A shares outstanding is an ongoing dilution data point to track against Bitcoin-per-share growth.

updates.headline: Warrant exercises begin, add $21.2M, diversify funding mix
updates.what_happened: CEO Matt Cole disclosed that warrant exercises began during the week and generated $21.2 million in gross proceeds, with SATA preferred sales supplying the remainder of capital for the latest BTC purchase. Including the warrant proceeds, SATA accounted for 57.7% of total capital raised for the week, a lower share than in prior all-preferred weeks.
updates.thesis_fit: Warrant exercises give Strive a second capital-raising lever beyond the daily-paying 13% SATA preferred, which can reduce dependence on high-cost preferred dividends versus existing shareholders over time.

entries.email_summary: ASST shares climb above $27 warrant strike as $718M PIPE warrant deadline nears Oct 13.
entries.bottom_line: The stock's move above the $27 PIPE warrant strike puts roughly $718M of potential fresh capital in play for further BTC purchases, but exercise would also add ~26.6M shares, so the net effect on Bitcoin-per-share depends on execution and timing. No new treasury purchases, financing terms, or governance changes emerged beyond items already reported.
source_conflicts: Reported ASST closing price on Sept 18, 2026 varies across sources: StockTitan cites $30.11/$30.13, MarketBeat cites prior close $28.28 with shares trading near $29.51, and Kraken cites a prior close of $28.32 with an intraday price near $30.02 — all consistent with a sharp single-day move but with imprecise agreement on the exact closing print.

Outstanding PIPE warrant notional is cited as 'more than $700 million' in early-September commentary versus a more precise $718 million figure disclosed by the CEO as of September 11, 2026 — likely the same instrument with rounding differences rather than a true conflict.

updates.headline: ASST shares clear $27 warrant strike; deadline moves to Oct 13
updates.what_happened: Strive's CEO disclosed that as of September 11, 2026 approximately $718 million in PIPE warrants with a $27 exercise price remained outstanding, and the exercise deadline was pushed from October 12 to 5:00 p.m. Eastern on October 13, 2026 because of the Columbus Day bank holiday, with all other terms unchanged. Separately, ASST shares closed at $30.11 on September 18, 2026, up sharply from a prior close near $28.28, putting the stock clearly above the $27 strike for the first time as the deadline approaches.
updates.thesis_fit: If warrant holders exercise, the roughly $718 million in proceeds tied to about 26.6 million shares could fund a large step-up in Bitcoin purchases, but the added share count is a direct dilution event whose net effect on Bitcoin-per-share depends on how quickly and profitably proceeds are deployed.

entries.email_summary: Strive added 469 BTC and held its 13% SATA dividend, though a leveraged ETF launch and the Clarity Act failure add volatility.
entries.bottom_line: Strive's small, steady BTC accumulation (469 BTC added Sept 8-11) and maintained 13% preferred dividend show continued financing discipline, keeping the BTC-per-share story intact. The Clarity Act failure and a new 2x leveraged retail ETF add near-term volatility unrelated to fundamentals.

updates.headline: Strive buys 469 BTC, holdings reach 25,000 BTC
updates.what_happened: Between September 8-11, Strive purchased 469 bitcoin at an average price of about $77,954, lifting total holdings from 24,531 to 25,000 BTC. Cash and cash equivalents rose slightly to $204.2 million over the same period.
updates.thesis_fit: Continued, modest BTC accumulation funded from cash rather than heavy dilution supports the BTC-per-share thesis.
updates.price_impact: No immediate effect; a routine accretive purchase consistent with prior weeks.

updates.headline: Strive maintains 13% SATA preferred dividend rate
updates.what_happened: Strive's board maintained the SATA perpetual preferred dividend rate at 13.00% for periods starting October 1, 2026, declaring daily cash dividends of $0.0516 per share for the month.
updates.thesis_fit: Stable preferred financing costs indicate the capital structure supporting BTC accumulation remains steady, without new dilution signals this period.
updates.price_impact: No immediate effect; routine capital-structure maintenance.

updates.headline: ASST falls over 5% as Clarity Act fails Senate vote
updates.what_happened: ASST shares declined more than 5% alongside broader crypto weakness after the Clarity Act failed a Senate procedural vote. Strive CEO Matt Cole called the outcome bad for the U.S. and crypto but said it may ultimately be good for Bitcoin.
updates.thesis_fit: A regulatory setback for the industry adds sentiment risk but does not alter Strive's underlying BTC-per-share execution.
updates.price_impact: Likely down short-term on risk-off crypto sentiment.

updates.headline: REX Shares launches 2x leveraged ASSX ETF on ASST
updates.what_happened: REX Shares launched ASSX, a T-REX 2X Long ETF targeting 200% of ASST's daily performance via swap agreements, designed for single-day trading. The product does not invest directly in Bitcoin and carries leverage, compounding, and liquidity risks.
updates.thesis_fit: A derivative product increases trading liquidity and speculative interest in ASST shares but has no direct effect on the company's BTC treasury or per-share metrics.
updates.price_impact: Likely increases intraday volatility in ASST without changing fundamental value.
